<description>
`AcceptToMemoryPool` and `ProcessNewPackage` end with `FlushStateToDisk(PERIODIC)`. Whether that flush writes depends on `m_next_write`, which lives in the static chainstate and is re-armed after each write. So the following targets leak the next write time from one input to the next:
- `tx_pool`
- `tx_pool_standard`
- `tx_package_eval`
- `ephemeral_package_eval`
- `validation_load_mempool`

Whether an input hits the write path (leveldb, block index, coins sync) then depends on the inputs that ran before it.
This matters because the fuzzer can then save an input for coverage that the input does not reproduce on its own, and a crash in that path may not reproduce from the single input that triggered it.

Fix it the same way `process_message(s)` and `cmpctblock` already do (#32822): call `DisableNextWrite()` at the start of each input.

Measured with `contrib/devtools/deterministic-fuzz-coverage --mode=combined` on qa-assets, comparing hits of the periodic-write branch (`validation.cpp:2839`, `nNow >= m_next_write`) between two shuffled replays:

| target | before (run A / run B) | after |
|--------|------------------------|-------|
| validation_load_mempool | 4 / 8 | 0 / 0 |
| tx_pool_standard | 9 / 5 | 0 / 0 |
| tx_pool | 4 / 17 | 0 / 0 |
| tx_package_eval | 6 / 7 | 0 / 0 |
| ephemeral_package_eval | 7 / 4 | 0 / 0 |

`validation_load_mempool` now passes the combined check. The other four still show unrelated nondeterminism, which this PR does not address:
- the script execution/signature cache shared across inputs;
- the `CoinsTip` cache state, which changes the number of `CCoinsViewDB` reads.

The input format is unchanged, so the qa-assets corpora stay valid.
</description>
